newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases to 3.05/3.10 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases to 3.05/3.10 pct.

text.p: German call money normalised on Thursday with call money rates easing to 3.05/10 percent, down from the rate of 4.50 percent they had hit at the end of 1996 as banks sought to meet their end-month reserve requirements.

The net drain on the repo by 8.4 billion marks, which took the market by surprise according to some market commentators, had not yet had any significant impact on the liquidity situation, dealers said.
The Bundesbank took market conditions into account when draining the repo, dealers said.

Commercial banks' effective deposits on December 30 were 48.9 billion marks, up from 45.1 billion marks, while the daily average for the month through December 30 grew to 40.8 billion marks from 40.5 billion marks.
Banks borrowed three billion marks in Lombard funds on December 31.
